speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the total number of applicants for the SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways Programme in 2020 and 2021; (b) among these, how many (i) have been successful in their application and (ii) found a permanent job after taking part in the programme; and (c) what is their median and average training allowance.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Government funds up to 90% of the training allowance.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: WSG also monitors the number of trainees who found a job within six months after completing or otherwise exiting the programme.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This is an encouraging sign that the attachments have equipped the trainees with useful skills, experience and industry contacts.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: For trainees who have not yet secured employment, WSG has proactively reached out to provide them with job search resources and information on job opportunities and upcoming job fairs.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Trainees can also take up WSG’s career matching services, which include career coaching, employability workshops and networking sessions to aid their job search.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The Member also asked about the number of applicants.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: SGUP applicants do not just make one application.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: Instead, they usually make multiple job and attachment applications and they choose the best offer that they can receive.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: The labour market started showing signs of recovery towards the end of 2020, with the resident unemployment rate improving steadily since the third quarter of 2020 and resident employment rising in 2020 and even more quickly in 2021.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: It is, therefore, not surprising that the majority of SGUP openings were not filled.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: SGUP remains a useful programme for employers and jobseekers who may face greater challenges in making a career switch.

speaker: The Minister for Manpower (Dr Tan See Leng)
text: This will provide more options for mature jobseekers looking to make a career switch.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Is the Minister saying that there were 20,000 applications for this SGUP programme but only 7,200 applicants were successful, of which, 3,400 completed the programme?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: If that is so, of the 20,000 applications, how many are the unique applicants?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: That means, we want to know what is the success rate of them getting a position under SGUP.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: The Minister was saying that only 3,400 have completed the programme.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: So, it appears that the drop-out rate is quite high.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng (West Coast)
text: Can the Minister enlighten us why that is so?

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: First, at the 20,800-applicant stage, these applicants do not just make one application to SGUP.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, when we are able to help them, that number comes down to about 7,200.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Out of the 7,200, close to 1,800 have exited the programme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: I think they have either moved on, found jobs or decided that they wanted to do something different and not continue with the programme itself.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: Out of the 5,000-plus that are left, the 2,600 or 77% that we have successfully placed into jobs that are permanent, the balance 800-plus we are still helping them in terms of working with them closely – as I have alluded to, an entire range of options of matching them with jobs, working with career counselling coaches, networking sessions and job fairs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: The balance 2,000 out of that 5,000 that exited, the 2,000 are still in the programme itself and they have not completed the programme.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: In an improving job situation, as we have seen in the last few quarters since the third quarter of 2020, we have, indeed, seen an uptick in terms of vacancies looking for job applicants to fill these vacancies.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: So, I suspect that that is what has led to the numbers dropping off.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: For the mid-career mature trainees, it is still a very important programme for us to continue and we think that the length of time that is taken to help them pivot, transform, upskill is something that is very useful and would take time for them to be comfortable in terms of taking on new roles and new jobs.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is not something that we can rush them into.

speaker: Dr Tan See Leng
text: It is taken against a larger context of the numbers that we are dealing with.
